From when I posted this to a reddit awhile back:

A few months back I was in need of some strings so I swung by my local guitar store to pick some up. As we all tend to do, I played a few guitars while I was there. It's a vintage store so they have a lot of guitars and amps from the 1950- all the way to the 1970. I ended up playing an amazing late 70's Es-335, a 1968 Rickenbacker 330a few 50s guilds and a Fender Esquire from like 1956 (with a $20,000 price tag). Anyway I put everything down to head to the counter and walk by this axe.

After playing upwards of $30k in vintage gear I picked this $300 Korean es-335 knockoff not expecting much. I've never really been interested in 335s anyway. Needless to say, I was utterly fucking blown away. I'm pretty picky when it come to my gear and I haven't bought a new guitar in almost 10 years but this thing felt right. After a bit I realized that I had been playing this thing for almost an hour and decided that I had to have it. The selling point for me was that it was not a Gibson scale length (24:75) but a longer 25.5. I was able to get it down to $275 with a really nice TKL hardshell case. This thing can do just about anything.

The guitar is a bit of a mystery. What I do know is it was part of the first run of Echotones, produced in Korea before they moved to china and then Indonesia. It's completely stock. It's apparently has a solid maple neck, back, sides, center block and top (surprisingly not laminate) w rosewood board. It has the aforementioned 25:5 scale, thus giving it a clearer sound (especially coupled with the maple) and some damn fine Duncan Desined '57 PAF pup knockoffs to top it off. The pots are good (may have been modified but I'm not sure). The only downside is the bridge is not wide enough for the strings to be over the pole pieces properly so a new TOM will be on order soon. The only problem being, I'm not sure which kind of replacement will actually work. It needs a new nut and the neck binding is a little shitty but I think I fixed that.

There are very few long scale hollow-bodies in the market, let alone at the price I paid (a custom Heritages and the Fender Starcaster are about it). When Hamer moved production to China and Indonesia the quality dropped significantly and specs changed to be more in line with a proper ES-335.

What are your favorite regional authors? That is, authors who primarily write from within the region you are from. For example, Seattle has JA Jance and New England has Stephen King.

Rob Thurman, from Indiana. She writes an Urban Fantasy series about a young man named Cal Leandros, his older half-brother Niko, and their shenanigans as freelance monster hunters in New York. Very "Supernatural", but the humor is darker, and to be honest, I just love Cal's snark and sarcasm. They're cheap, fun little reads and I enjoy the hell out of them!
